customer.customer.listingDetail.listingExperience: 07:30 – 08:00 – Our guide will meet you at your hotel/stay and start a 120km comfortable Limousine bus journey through the verdant landscape. Stopover for a rest on the way.
10:30 – Arrive Bai Dinh pagoda complex, get on electric cars to visit massive architecture.
12:15 – Enjoy the buffet lunch at our restaurant, a great place to savor the flavours of Vietnamese food.
13:30 – Visit Trang An Grottoes, get on a rowing boat traveling along the river with scenic mountain and green fields landscape.
15:45 – Arrive at Mua Cave and start an amazing trek up to the top of Ngoa Long mountain.
17:30 – 20:00 – Return to our Limousine bus and then come back to Hanoi. Drop you off at your hotel/stay. Other things to note
Any experience can be canceled and fully refunded within 24 hours of purchase, or at least 7 days before the experience starts.

content.content.postBody.bai-bien-my-khe.s1p1: My Khe is Da Nang's main beach, just east of the city. Travel guides describe a curve of fine white sand stretching towards the Marble Mountains; the beach can also be seen to the south from the Son Tra Peninsula.
content.content.postBody.bai-bien-my-khe.s1p2: Several travel sites say that Forbes (US) once listed My Khe among the most attractive beaches on the planet in 2005. That is what those sites report; we have not checked it against the original Forbes article.
content.content.postBody.bai-bien-my-khe.s2p1: Early morning and late afternoon are usually more pleasant for a walk on the sand. Some travel guides note that the dry season in Da Nang runs from about February to the end of August, while from October to December the city can be affected by storms.
content.content.postBody.bai-bien-my-khe.s2p2: Before going into the water, check the weather forecast and follow the lifeguards' instructions on the beach.
content.content.postBody.bai-bien-my-khe.s3p1: Sources give very different lengths for My Khe: some measure the whole coastal strip, others only the developed section. For that reason this article gives no figure.
content.content.postBody.ban-dao-son-tra.s1p1: Vietnam Tourism suggests taking the bends of the peninsula slowly to enjoy the views and, if time allows, driving the full loop along the coast. From Son Tra you can see My Khe beach to the south and the Hai Van Pass to the north.
content.content.postBody.ban-dao-son-tra.s2p1: Linh Ung is a large pagoda and a landmark of Da Nang, often visited when going around Son Tra. All sources give the height of the white Guanyin statue here as 67 m.
content.content.postBody.ban-dao-son-tra.s3p1: Son Tra is a nature reserve and home to the red-shanked douc langur. Sources disagree on the size of the reserve and the number of langurs, so this article gives no figures.
content.content.postBody.ban-dao-son-tra.s3p2: This is wildlife territory: stay quiet and do not disturb the animals. As at the beach, some guides note that storms can occur from October to December, so check the forecast before heading up the peninsula.
content.content.postBody.cau-rong-song-han.s1p1: According to Wikipedia, construction of the Dragon Bridge began on 19 July 2009 and it opened to traffic on 29 March 2013. The steel bridge is 666 m long and 37.5 m wide, with six lanes.
content.content.postBody.cau-rong-song-han.s2h: The dragon breathes fire and water
content.content.postBody.cau-rong-song-han.s2p1: The bridge was designed to breathe fire and water on Saturday and Sunday evenings at 9 pm. That is the design intent stated on Wikipedia; we could not confirm the current schedule, so please check the city's latest announcement before you go.
content.content.postBody.cau-rong-song-han.s3p1: The Han River bank near the Han River Port is also where the fireworks of the Da Nang International Fireworks Festival are launched; the report on the 2026 festival season is in the Travel news section.
content.content.postBody.co-do-hue.s1p1: The Complex of Hue Monuments was inscribed by UNESCO in 1993. According to Wikipedia it includes the Imperial City, the Citadel and the Forbidden Purple City, as well as works outside the walls such as the tombs of seven emperors, pagodas and temples.
content.content.postBody.co-do-hue.s2p1: Hue was chosen as the capital of the unified Vietnam in 1802, under Emperor Gia Long.
content.content.postBody.co-do-hue.s3p1: Hue lies north of the Hai Van Pass, and Vietnam Tourism has a separate article about the journey from Hoi An to Hue over this pass. This article gives no travel time, opening hours or ticket prices because they change; check the site's official channels when you plan your trip.
content.content.postBody.diff-2026-khep-lai.s1p1: According to the Government's online newspaper, the 2026 Da Nang International Fireworks Festival ran from 30 May to 11 July 2026 along the Han River bank, with six performance nights on Saturday evenings. The nights' themes were, in turn, Nature, Heritage, Culture, Creativity, Vision and, on the final night, "Horizons Connected". The schedule, themes and competing teams for each night were announced before the festival; this article uses only the parts of the reports that confirm what took place.
content.content.postBody.diff-2026-khep-lai.s2p1: Also according to the Government's online newspaper (12 July 2026), on the final night of 11 July the Portuguese team won the championship and China came second; the "Creativity" prize went to Italy, the "Promising" prize to Japan and the "Audience Favourite" prize to the Da Nang team. We have read these results in only one source. The reports disagree on the number of participating teams, so this article gives no figure.
content.content.postBody.diff-2026-khep-lai.s3p1: According to the Da Nang Department of Culture, Sports and Tourism, as relayed by Van Hoa newspaper, the city received about 2.72 million overnight guests during the festival season (30 May–11 July 2026), up nearly 45% on the 2025 season. This figure was published by the regulator and has not been independently verified.
content.content.postBody.diff-2026-khep-lai.s3p2: The article's photograph is an archive picture of spectators watching fireworks at the festival, not a specific night of 2026.
content.content.postBody.du-lich-da-nang-9-thang: VietnamPlus, citing VNA statistics, reports that accommodation providers in Da Nang served about 15.86 million guests in the first nine months of 2026, up 26.4% year on year.

Revenue from accommodation and food services reached about 52,945 billion VND, up 26.2%; of this, accommodation was about 16,939 billion VND (up 23.9%) and food services about 36,006 billion VND (up 27.3%). Revenue from travel services was about 4,028 billion VND, up 16.5%.

These are the city's statistics for all accommodation providers, not information about The BHA's availability or prices. Real room availability and prices come from the booking system for the dates you choose.

content.content.postBody.ngu-hanh-son.s1p1: The Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) are five limestone mountains named after the five elements: Metal, Water, Wood, Fire and Earth. They lie south of central Da Nang; Vietnam Tourism gives about seven km from the centre and says you can go by taxi.
content.content.postBody.ngu-hanh-son.s2p1: Thuy Son is the best-known peak, with many caves holding Hindu and Buddhist shrines. According to Wikipedia it is the only one open to visitors, with a 156-step staircase to the top and panoramic views.
content.content.postBody.ngu-hanh-son.s2p2: The photograph for this article shows the coast seen from the mountain.
content.content.postBody.ngu-hanh-son.s3p1: The area around the mountains is famous for stone carving. Some travel guides advise arriving early in the day to avoid the crowds; opening hours and ticket prices can change, so check the latest notice at the ticket office.
content.content.postBody.pho-co-hoi-an.s1p1: Hoi An Ancient Town was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on 4 December 1999 under criteria (ii) and (v): it is evidence of cultural exchange in a trading port and a well-preserved traditional Asian trading port.
content.content.postBody.pho-co-hoi-an.s2h: From Da Nang to Hoi An
content.content.postBody.pho-co-hoi-an.s2p1: Vietnam Tourism says Hoi An is about 45 minutes by road from Da Nang and is known for its alleys, pagodas and old shophouses. Actual travel time depends on traffic and how you travel.
content.content.postBody.pho-co-hoi-an.s3p1: In the evening the old town lights its lanterns, as in this article's photograph. A few events are planned here for late 2026; you can read the roundup in the Travel news section, and remember that schedules may change.
content.content.postBody.su-kien-cuoi-nam-2026.s: Vietnam Cultural Heritage Day in the Hoi An old quarter, 23 November to 7 December 2026: exhibitions, a cross-country run, Bai Choi performances and free entry to the old town.

Da Nang International Lantern Festival 2026, 3 to 6 December 2026 in the wards of Hoi An, Hoi An Dong and Hoi An Tay. Another event listing once gave 21–25 January for this festival, so wait for the official announcement before booking.
Da Nang New Year Festival 2027, planned from December 2026 to January 2027 in squares, landscaped spaces, pedestrian streets and on the beach.
From the Van Hoa newspaper report (5 September 2026)
The events below are plans reported by the newspaper in early September; they had not yet taken place at that time.
Da Nang Christmas Market 2026: 4–6 December 2026 at the Ariyana Convention Centre Da Nang.
Christmas celebration 2026: 24–25 December 2026 in the Hoi An old quarter.
From the Danang FantastiCity events list
This page was posted on 1 December 2025 and labels the whole events table "expected dates" and "information subject to change depending on actual circumstances".
These are not events organised by The BHA. Check the organisers' latest announcements before booking accommodation or tickets.
